These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Round monetary Decimal results only via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with the established codes: "invalid_state" for wrong invoice status, "invalid_quantity" for bad quantity, "negative_amount" for negative money.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money via to_money and round_money: Never store raw unit_price values on LineItem; pass them through to_money() and round_money() from ledgerly.money before constructing the line, and compare against ZERO for sign checks.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool when validating integer inputs: When validating integer parameters, explicitly reject bool with isinstance(x, bool) before the int check, since True/False are ints in Python.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly modules, normalize incoming datetimes with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic, rather than assuming tz-awareness.
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
